newsitem.title: CHINA: Power project started at China oil refinery.
newsitem.headline: Power project started at China oil refinery.

text.p: A Japan-sponsored project aimed at producing electric power from Chinese oil refineries has been put into operation, the Overseas Edition of the People's Daily said on Wednesday.

The project, set up by Japan's New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organisation (NEDO) at the Shengli plant of the Qilu Petrochemical Co in eastern China's Shandong province, had been successfully tested, the newspaper said.

It had the capacity to generate 42,000 megawatt-hours of electricity a year using heat generated by the oil refining process. At the same time it would recover almost 1,000 tonnes of chemical catalysts, benefitting the plant economically and protecting the environment, it said.
The project was intended to find ways to apply advanced Japanese power recovery technology at refineries using Chinese equipment, it said, but gave no other details.
NEDO, which is backed by Japan's Ministry of International Trade and Industry, opened a representative office in Beijing earlier this year.
